version: production e23daec baseline and local stage06 working-tree build; see experimentVersions
scope: Real-device RAF/CPU observations, completed temporary ablations and a bounded sanitized WebContent thermal-signal alignment. No direct GPU timer, native CPU/GPU clock, physical temperature or ProcessInfo thermal grade was measured. Visual ablations intentionally alter rendering and are diagnostics only. Three renderer.info counts are application-requested and may differ from intercepted GPU submissions. Raw system logs with device/process identifiers are excluded from this archive.

streaming-upload.interpretation: Suppressing all observed bufferSubData uploads for 12 seconds did not restore RAF (11.64 / 11.65 / 11.57 Hz). No texImage2D or texSubImage2D calls in these phases. Same moon/night camera and state; not a frame-time GPU measurement.

default-framebuffer-msaa.interpretation: Actual antialias:false context still reaches 12 Hz by navigation +48.9s. On/off captures are separate runs with different prior paths, durations and sound states, so do not derive a relative AA speedup. In the off run, steady breeze degradation occurred with stable Three programs/textures/geometries 81/136/266. Full off-run bounded workload included to retain the onset.

finish.interpretation: 158 gl.finish calls measured about 1 ms in JavaScript total; this is not GPU time. WebKit current main forwards finish through ordinary asynchronous IPC send, and GPUProcess performs the actual finish. This source mechanism is consistent with quick JS return, but has not been mapped to the exact iOS 26.6.2 build. No sustained RAF improvement.

readback.interpretation: One-pixel synchronous readback measured 122 calls /7687 ms (~63.0 ms/call), including synchronization, IPC and readback costs rather than pure GPU execution. User camera/view and viewport changed; every phase has cameraStable:false. Do not compare before/after RAF as a controlled effect or present readback as an optimization.

wind-short.limitations: Diagnostic shader ablation changes plant positions/coverage and active GPU inputs. CPU wind, uploads, geometry, material fragment hooks, light settings and draw submission remain in place. Results do not isolate ALU from all resulting GPU work.
wind-short.interpretation: The 12-second no-sway stage reached 27.71 Hz, but no-leaf and both remained 9.68/10.61 Hz. Temporary gains were inconsistent and were followed by the sustained test. No official wind shader was changed.

wind-long.limitations: Diagnostic shader ablation changes plant positions/coverage and active GPU inputs. CPU wind, uploads, geometry, material fragment hooks, light settings and draw submission remain in place. Results do not isolate ALU from all resulting GPU work.
wind-long.sampleInterval: approximately 1 second, each raf object is the existing rolling 5-second window
wind-long.interpretation: Completed 8s baseline /60s no-sway /35s restore: final windows 10.67 /9.88 /10.08 Hz. No sustained benefit from removing sway. Texture/Buffer/Framebuffer/Renderbuffer remained158/1346/59/1; temporary shader variants changed Program149->180 and VAO1103->1281, and Program returned149 after probe clone cleanup. Counts are handles, not bytes or complete driver memory.

minimal-draw.method: Preserve the original draw invocation flow, but intercept drawElements/drawArrays and their instanced variants: cap element/vertex count at 3 and instance count at 1. No calls are skipped. Restore original methods after the completed sequence.
minimal-draw.countsSemantics: counts.calls is the cumulative intercepted draw invocation count during the 15-second phase, not a fixed calls-per-second rate. counts.vertices sums the post-interception element/vertex count arguments, not unique vertex shader executions. The instances field was initialized but never incremented, so its zero is not a measured instance count.
minimal-draw.rendererCountCaveat: Three renderer drawCalls/triangles remain application-requested counts before low-level interception. In particular, the recorded 9,247,343 triangles during the minimal phase were NOT the actually submitted triangle count.
minimal-draw.conclusion: 9.90 Hz baseline -> 59.99 Hz after 15 seconds of at-most-three-vertices/one-instance drawing -> 10.32 Hz after 35 seconds restored. Actual per-draw work materially affects throughput even with the original invocation flow. Geometry collapse also changes primitive processing and fragment coverage, so this does not isolate a vertex shader function or establish a no-visual-loss fix.

all-framebuffer-scissor.method: Force scissor to a single pixel for all framebuffers, including default, shadow and offscreen targets; leave vertex/index/instance draw arguments unchanged. Restore the original scissor methods and state after the completed sequence.
all-framebuffer-scissor.conclusion: 10.15 Hz baseline -> 15.15 Hz after 45 seconds of all-framebuffer one-pixel coverage -> 11.30 Hz after 35 seconds restored. Restricting pixel coverage alone does not restore 60 Hz. Together with minimal drawing, this supports investigating geometry/primitive processing and associated GPU/driver cost, without providing per-stage GPU timing.

thermal-alignment.kind: bounded observational time alignment, not an ablation or controlled thermal intervention
thermal-alignment.timezone: Asia/Shanghai (+08:00); the device log has local timestamps without an offset

selection.exclusionReason: Float32 geometry conversion began only after the baseline ended at 90.137s. The baseline samples and events list include only 0-80s; a later thermal-disabled event is explicitly separated in postWindowObservation.

thermal-alignment.redaction: Only selected thermal booleans, local timestamps, relative times, application state and numerical workload fields are retained. Process IDs, process UUIDs, memory addresses, device paths and unrelated system log messages are omitted. Raw files remain local and must not be committed.

resourcesAfterSceneReady.note: The two draw/triangle totals reflect alternating shadow frames, not resource growth. Startup samples before 5.962s are retained separately with zero renderer counts.

webkitSourceInterpretation.interpretation: Current main only adjusts rendering update frequency in handleThermalMitigationChange when aggressive response is enabled; half-speed animation reasons include AggressiveThermalMitigation, not ordinary ThermalMitigation. Ordinary thermal mitigation can still change DOM timer alignment. The observed event has aggressive=false. These sources are not mapped to the exact iOS build and do not rule out other system/GPU power management.

thermal-alignment.conclusion: The WebContent process received a thermal mitigation enabled signal at 33.704s. RAF had already declined from 31.90Hz at 22.069s to 27.50Hz at 23.087s, 15.78Hz at 24.101s and 10.92Hz at 27.227s. The notification therefore follows the observed decline by roughly 10 seconds; this establishes a thermal-management signal in the same run, not that it caused the onset or directly locked RAF to 10Hz. Observed geometry, texture and program counts remain stable; no native temperature or GPU/CPU clock was obtained. A later separate observation at 128.703s reports thermal mitigation disabled while the Float32 representation diagnostic was still around 11Hz; after restoring original attributes for 35 seconds the phase ended at 11.61Hz. This further contradicts a direct on/off RAF thermal lock, with no native clock evidence.

postWindowObservation.note: This event is outside the 0-80 second unchanged-geometry baseline and is retained separately. The experimental geometry representation was active; RAF stayed around 11Hz and remained 11.61Hz after the final 35-second restoration.

float32-static-attributes.scope: Representation-only diagnostic: original index, groups, vertex count, material/shaders, instance data, dynamic wind/rain attributes retained. Static normalized/integer or interleaved position/normal/uv/color becomes Float32 through normalized accessors. Finite-precision input rounding may differ; no geometry or density simplification.
float32-static-attributes.retention: Only completed phase summaries, aggregate coverage and the six process samples around the thermal-disabled event are retained; raw input is hashed below.
float32-static-attributes.countCaveat: Temporary geometry clones raised the geometry and GL buffer/VAO counts during the diagnostic. This is deliberate probe allocation, not growth of the unmodified baseline. All 204 clones were disposed at cleanup; only the post-cleanup program count was recorded, so no post-cleanup geometry total is inferred.
float32-static-attributes.conclusion: Expanding static attributes to Float32 did not restore throughput: 10.93Hz baseline, 11.32Hz after 60 seconds converted, 11.61Hz after 35 seconds restored. Thermal mitigation became false during the converted phase, with adjacent samples still about 11Hz. This is contrary to a simple on/off WebKit RAF thermal lock, but does not rule out other GPU/system power management.

rain-memory-released-baseline.version: local stage06 build including release of one-time rain baking query/index data; same presentation settings
rain-memory-released-baseline.limitation: The 74,565,832-byte / 71.11MiB figure is the measured source TypedArray capacity made reclaimable by releasing references, not a phone RSS/GPU-memory measurement or proof of immediate GC. The initial startup state has place=null before courtyard is ready.
rain-memory-released-baseline.conclusion: The fixed rain-data retention was removed, but the same deterioration persisted: 32.42Hz at 22.693s, 25.64Hz at 23.707s, 16.88Hz at 24.714s, 12.66Hz at 25.741s and 11.37Hz at 26.796s. At 80.788s the last-five-second RAF window was 11.607Hz. This refutes treating the released rain index as sufficient to resolve the observed slowdown.

startup-fence.endedBecause: Reached the bounded 600 completed-sample cap before the nominal 70-second collection duration.
startup-fence.method: After a main-scene render, insert at most one pending WebGL2 fenceSync and gl.flush; poll clientWaitSync(sync,0,0) with an 8ms setTimeout request until signaled. Delete each sync and restore renderer.render on completion. No frame geometry, material or setting change is part of this diagnostic.
startup-fence.limitation: Fence latency includes command queue, cross-process IPC, GPU execution and JS polling delay. It is not a pure GPU timer. Explicit flush, repeated IPC queries, JavaScript callbacks and snapshot reads can perturb scheduling; this is an instrumented run. One pending fence at a time means samples do not represent every frame, and each fence covers previously queued commands rather than an isolated frame GPU time.
startup-fence.windowSelection: Include only fences issued and completed wholly inside each comparison window. RAF uses only complete workload buckets inside that window, aggregating count*1000/observedMs. Percentiles use linear interpolation of sorted samples; poll intervals include the first issue-to-poll interval.
startup-fence.excludedChanges: The capture completed before the later LOD data injection. No LOD data/geometry changes are included.
startup-fence.conclusion: RAF falls from 32.66Hz to 11.43Hz between the defined windows while median observed fence completion latency rises from 35ms to 85ms (p95 36ms to 101ms). Median polling intervals stay 9ms and each clientWaitSync call is at most 1ms; late samples repeatedly report TIMEOUT_EXPIRED until a median 71ms after issue. This supports increased unfinished GL-work/IPC completion latency, not a single 85ms JavaScript polling pause. It does not isolate GPU execution, prove queue growth or distinguish GPU power state from driver/IPC behavior. The probe preserves the same approximately 23-27s deterioration despite its instrumentation.

hot-fence.limitation: Fence latency includes command queue, cross-process IPC, GPU execution and JS polling delay. It is not a pure GPU timer. This earlier hot-state probe did not record each poll timestamp, fence creation duration or flush duration; those details come only from the separate startup run.

index-lod-diagnostic.version: local stage06 with rain-memory release; temporary index-only LOD diagnostic, not production
index-lod-diagnostic.scope: Temporary lossy diagnostic: 30mm attribute-aware model index simplification; optional complete-leaf subsets change foliage density. Original vertices/attributes/materials/wind/instance data retained. Actual workload counts scene render submissions including its shadows, not GPU execution time.
index-lod-diagnostic.method: Strict source-asset name/count/index fingerprint matching; model index simplification configured to 0.03 world metres, followed by an optional whole-leaf subset stage. Original vertex attributes, materials, wind/instance data and source indices retain identity. Final cleanup restores original geometry assignments and renderer hooks and disposes temporary geometry clones.

coverage.limits: Only strict asset-name + vertex count + source-index FNV fingerprint matches. Index reduction does not reduce vertex-buffer allocations. Projection/camera/visibility still determine actual work; prototype sums are not draw counts.

index-lod-diagnostic.windowDefinition: For each completed stable-camera phase, use only recorded consecutive intervals entirely inside its final 10 seconds; sum submission counts and observed durations. RAF in phaseResults is a separate last-5-second browser callback window. Beauty triangles per submitted frame are directly comparable; alternating-shadow totals can vary with frame parity.
index-lod-diagnostic.excludedMisleadingMetric: The raw triangleReductionFromBaseline compares whole phases with the initial, different camera/projection/output size. It is intentionally omitted from this archive and must not be reported as a controlled reduction.
limitations: The user moved the camera during the model stage; drawing size also changed from 603x1071 to 603x1131. Initial 11.42Hz cannot be used as a controlled comparator for the later camera.

The model final 98 recorded snapshots, all 120 leaf-stage snapshots, all 35 restore snapshots and final phase results match the final camera/world matrix/projection/state/output exactly. Snapshots do not prove no unobserved movement between samples.

These are sequential stages on one already-slow phone. Thermal and native GPU-clock state were not controlled or measured. The finite improvement does not establish which driver/system layer causes the time-dependent slowdown.

Model simplification and removing whole leaves alter visible geometry; this is a lossy diagnostic with no equivalence or visual acceptance claim. It is not implemented as a default or user configuration.

Index simplification keeps original vertex-buffer allocations and temporarily adds index storage and geometry wrappers. Geometry count includes temporary clones before cleanup; only Program count was captured after cleanup, not a complete post-cleanup resource snapshot.
index-lod-diagnostic.conclusion: At the fixed later camera, completed model and model+leaf stages end at 13.03Hz and 14.66Hz, then original geometry restoration ends at 11.50Hz. This is a finite improvement without a return to smooth 30/60Hz; it does not solve the mobile problem or justify claiming a product LOD optimization.

native-process-baseline.version: local stage06 with rain-memory release, before static-idle render gating; no LOD probe active
native-process-baseline.method: Read-only DVT sysmontap via userspace transport, nominally two native samples per second. Parent confirmed normal collector exit. A streaming filter read the completed private JSONL once; only Safari, WebContent, WebKit GPU, SpringBoard and thermal-service metrics were selected. No device paths, process IDs, start-clock identities or other applications are archived.
native-process-baseline.transportResolution: The earlier --native attempt ended in host macOS Python/XPC teardown with SIGKILL/137, not a phone process crash. --userspace succeeded without downloading or mounting a developer disk image.

processAttribution.basis: The parent observed a single active WebContent in the private process inventory; the same native process lifetime spans page reload, and its CPU/memory changes align with that reload. Two other observed WebContent processes report zero median CPU in all three measurement windows.
processAttribution.certainty: Strong candidate, not an authoritative inspected Safari-tab-to-process association.
processAttribution.gpuScope: WebKit GPU is a shared browser process; its metrics are not exclusive page costs.

metricDefinitions.cpuUsage: Reported native sysmontap cpuUsage value; no normalization or GPU-utilization interpretation is applied.
metricDefinitions.physFootprintBytes: Native per-process physFootprint; not JS heap or dedicated GPU-memory usage.
metricDefinitions.startTimeNativeTicks: startAbsTime native opaque clock value, not a wall-clock epoch.
metricDefinitions.timestamp: Timestamp present on each collector output record; alignment can include transport/host logging delay.

limitations: Native CPU usage, RSS, physical footprint and compressed bytes are process-level measurements, not GPU execution time, GPU watts, GPU utilization, CPU/GPU clocks, physical temperature or ProcessInfo thermal grade. powerScore is intentionally not interpreted or archived as power.
Timestamp alignment uses the native collector record timestamps and browser navigation timeOrigin; transport or host logging delay can affect fine-grained alignment.
Native sampling and remote inspection can perturb the run; this navigation starts around 25Hz, unlike the separate fence navigation around 32Hz. Do not combine them into a single A/B benchmark.
RSS and physFootprint have different accounting and may include shared or mapped memory; do not add processes or these fields to estimate exclusive webpage memory.
The selected process memory does not rise monotonically as RAF declines; that does not prove zero leaks, no internal churn or no driver/GPU allocation issue.
The native trace ends around navigation107s. The browser capture at175.785s is retained only as an explicitly later observation, not paired with simultaneous native data.
Thermal-service process activity is not a thermal-state reading. No hardware clock or power conclusion follows from this experiment.
native-process-baseline.conclusion: This navigation slows around23-28s with fixed page state and renderer resources. Candidate WebContent and WebKit GPU CPU values decrease with the lower frame rate while their RSS/physical-footprint measurements remain broadly stable after loading. There is no measured steadily growing process-memory trend matching the decline. The root cause and a sustained full-quality mobile fix remain unresolved.

ios-runtime-system.jsonl.hashScope: Byte sequence read for this bounded extraction; if the live log later appends, verify the first bytesAtCapture bytes.

native-page-baseline-150s.jsonl.privacy: Private all-process trace; only bounded whitelisted metrics are archived.

currentConclusion: Stage06 resource housekeeping does not resolve sustained outdoor 10-13Hz. Minimal per-draw geometry restored 59.99Hz for 15s and full drawing returned to 10.32Hz after 35s; all-framebuffer one-pixel coverage reached only 15.15Hz after 45s. A later unchanged-workload run captured a WebContent thermal-mitigation transition at 33.704s, while RAF had already dropped during 23-27s with stable textures/geometries/programs. Thermal-management signaling is now observed, but its timing does not prove it triggered the onset or directly capped RAF to 10Hz. No native clock/temperature evidence or full-quality fix has been established. The same thermal flag later turned off at 128.703s without frame-rate recovery; final restoration after the Float32 attribute probe was still 11.61Hz. A simple WebKit RAF thermal lock therefore does not explain both transitions. Releasing the fixed 71.11MiB rain-baking TypedArrays also did not prevent the 23-27s decline or restore the 80s window (11.607Hz). A completed startup fence diagnostic found median observed completion latency 35ms at navigation10-20s vs85ms at35-65s, with stable9ms median polling and single polls<=1ms. This localizes a growing completion wait beyond simply delayed JavaScript polling, but is not a pure GPU timer or an established driver/thermal cause. A later temporary, lossy index-LOD trial reached 13.03Hz for models and 14.66Hz with whole-leaf subsets, then 11.50Hz after original-geometry restoration at the same later camera/projection/output; it did not restore smoothness. The initial 11.42Hz baseline had a different camera and output size and is not a controlled comparison. A subsequent completed150s userspace native process trace measured CPU/RSS/physFootprint. During the aligned page slowdown, candidate WebContent and shared WebKit GPU process memory stayed broadly stable after loading while reported CPU usage fell; no steadily growing process-memory trend was measured. These are not GPU watt/clock measurements and do not establish a full-quality fix.

systemMeasurementLimitations.gpuTimer: EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 was unavailable on this phone.
systemMeasurementLimitations.dvtSysmon: The earlier --native host Python/XPC path ended during macOS teardown with SIGKILL/137; it was not evidence of a phone crash. A subsequent --userspace DVT sysmontap collection completed normally and measured native process CPU usage, RSS, physFootprint, compressed bytes and thread count without downloading or mounting a developer image. These measurements still provide no GPU/CPU clocks, GPU watts or physical temperature.
systemMeasurementLimitations.power: The phone was connected to the Mac during testing; these observations do not establish behavior on battery alone.
systemMeasurementLimitations.classicSyslog: Classic syslog eventually succeeded. Selected WebContent messages show thermal mitigation false at navigation+4.109s, true at +33.704s, followed by Page thermal=true/aggressive=false. This signal does not provide a clock, physical temperature or ProcessInfo thermal grade, and occurred after the frame-rate decline had started. A later selected Page event at +128.703s sets both booleans false, but adjacent RAF samples remain about 11Hz and the completed restored phase ends at 11.61Hz.
